title: Ishtaria datadisk
description: Definitions for the files of a story datadisk. A datadisk directory holds datadisk.yaml (manifest), places/*.yaml, npcs/*.yaml, dialogues/*.yaml, quests/*.yaml, lore/*.yaml and i18n/<language>.yaml. Each file is validated against the definition named by its directory; $defs/manifest validates datadisk.yaml.

local_id.description: Identifier unique inside one datadisk; the loader qualifies it as <disk>:<id>.

wildlife_entry.description: One scenery or fauna catalog id with a relative weight for a place wildlife overlay.

id.description: An id from the server's world_objects.json or world_fauna.json catalogs (for example nature.tree_palmTall).

waterside.description: When true, this fauna (or flora) only spawns within about 60 m of patch water, a river, or the sea. Default false.

ref.description: Reference to a local id, or to <disk>:<id> of a declared dependency.

text_key.description: Translation key; the text lives in i18n/<language>.yaml.

status.description: draft = generated and not yet reviewed; release builds reject drafts.

format.description: Datadisk format version this disk follows (DATADISK-SPEC.md); 1 when absent.

cover.description: Cover image (png or jpg, at most 1 MiB) that clients show when they connect to a server using the disk.

loading_marker.description: Image (png, at most 1 MiB) the client's loading bar draws at the bar's current value. Without it the engine's bar only differs in colour between the finished and the remaining part. The figure should face right: the bar fills from left to right.

cover_music.description: Track id from music/*.yaml played once while the cover image is shown (logo jingle; prefer loop: false).

ambient_music.description: Track id from music/*.yaml played as the default background when the player is outside every place music radius (e.g. plains travel).

player_character.description: The character every new player of a world using this disk plays, as <pack>/<skin> of the character creator (for example protagonists/criminalMaleA). Players then choose only their nickname; the first disk in the order of application that sets it wins. Existing players keep their character. Without it players choose a look.

player_model.description: A glTF binary below media/models/ (<= 4 MiB, in metres, +Y up, a skeleton with clips named Idle and Walk, and optionally Run, Jump, Sit, Swim, Die) that clients draw for the player_character instead of its pack look, which stays the fallback while the model loads. Requires player_character.

ordinal_numerals.description: How clients write the number of a life under one login on a memorial (the second life of a login is II). roman is the engine default; sumerian writes cuneiform numerals (U+12079 = 1, U+1230B = 10, base 60) and requires ordinal_font.

ordinal_font.description: A .ttf or .otf below media/fonts/ (<= 1 MiB) with the glyphs of ordinal_numerals; clients fetch it from the server's media route.

settlement_houses.description: The houses of the towns and villages the generator builds in a world using this disk: models of the disk, scaled to a plot drawn from the ranges and turned to the plaza, instead of the engine's low-poly kit houses (its temples and towers are then left out too).

native_m.description: Width, height and depth of the model in its own units.

ground.description: The ground set clients draw the land with, one the client has textures for: alluvial (dry silt plain between two rivers: steppe grass, silt, cracked mud, sand and dirt from Poly Haven). Without it the default ground is drawn. Servers announce it in /world datadisks.

ground_layers.description: Which ground layers the client draws each land biome with, laid over the `ground` set: the key is a land biome (lowland, grassland, temperate_forest, mountain, polar), `beach` or `scree`; the value is one to three layers (base, alternate and accent ground; a beach or scree takes the first). Layers are the folders of the client's assets/terrain (Poly Haven, CC0), named in the server's GROUND_LAYERS. Servers announce it in /world datadisks.

astronomy.description: When and on which planet the story happens, so that the sky is the right one: the tilt of the axis, the turn of the planet and the precession of the star field. Every field is optional and defaults to today's Earth. Servers apply it to the sun and moon and announce it in /world solar; clients draw the sky from it.

year.description: The astronomical year the story is set in (2700 BCE is -2699). The tilt of the axis (Laskar 2004) and the precession of the star field (Capitaine 2003) are those of that year. -9000..11000.

obliquity_deg.description: The tilt of the planet's axis in degrees, instead of the one the year gives (another planet, or a chosen sky). 0..60.

sidereal_day_seconds.description: One turn of the planet against the stars, in seconds (today's Earth 86164.0905).

player_body.description: The body of the player_character: how tall it stands and how much more than a man it endures. Clients draw the character that tall (the creator's people are 1.8 m) and the server hurts it less when it falls: the drop counts against the body's size and the damage is divided by toughness. Requires player_character.

starting_items.description: Items granted once when a new player record is created on a world using this disk (never on login or reconnect).

auto_start_quests.description: Local quest ids started at character creation (stage = the quest's start_stage).

world.description: The real planet a world using this disk is generated on (maximum historical fidelity). Only one selected disk may define it; the world's heightmap strip is then rendered from these maps by ishtaria-worldgen --earth instead of the procedural noise.

heightmap.description: Equirectangular relief of the whole planet as a binary P5 PGM (16-bit, maxval 65535, big-endian; width = 2 x height), row 0 at +90 degrees, column 0 at -180 degrees. A pixel is the elevation in metres as a signed 16-bit value: 0 is sea level, land is positive, bathymetry is negative. The worldgen strips it onto the cube-sphere with latitude = asin(y) and longitude = atan2(-z, x), so the server's compass is the real north of the planet.

water.description: Water mask of the same size (P5, 8-bit, maxval 255): 0 is land, 255 is water (sea, lakes, rivers). It overrides the heights at the coastline: water never rises above sea level and land never sinks below it, so shallow seas (the Persian Gulf) stay sea and dry depressions (Qattara) stay land however the 8-bit strip quantises them. Rivers and reconstructed historical shorelines live here.

biomes.description: Optional land biomes painted over the planet; whatever the disk leaves out the world generator decides itself. Water is never painted.

map.description: Equirectangular P5 PGM of the size of the heightmap (8-bit, maxval 255, row 0 at +90 degrees, column 0 at -180 degrees). A pixel is 0 where the generator decides, or a land biome: 3 lowland, 4 grassland, 5 temperate_forest, 6 mountain, 7 polar. Painted pixels replace the derived biome of land cells only: sea, lakes and rivers still follow the relief.

condition.description: Structured condition. No scripting: exactly one key.

effect.description: Structured effect applied by the server in one transaction.

once.description: Apply the nested effects only the first time this key is used by a player.

flourish.description: Visual duel / flourish clips played by the client (no damage). Returned with the dialogue reply.

set_playable.description: Hand the player another body (pack character, optional datadisk model, optional NPC to hide while playing as them).

teleport_place.description: Move the player to a placed story place (abstracted epic travel). Qualified on load.

sky_ship.description: Id of a ship of the disk's sky_flyers.yaml: the ship crosses the player's view (an event the client draws) and the player earns the ship's achievement.

reveal_places.description: Tell the player of places (ids of places of the disk, qualified on load): from then on they stay on the map and compass, like the places of begun quests. A character who says where something lies.

places.description: places/*.yaml: a list of anchors the world generator must find a spot for.

parent.description: The place this one stands inside or beside; placed after it, within radius_m.

preset.description: pasture: only a flock of sheep and goats and the shepherd who drives it from a fold beside the place to a pasture and back, for a place whose buildings the disk lists itself.

structure.description: A building of the datadisk itself, drawn at the place and walkable by its mesh (stairs up to 0.45 m per step, arches, platforms). Excludes scenery.

model.description: A self-contained glTF binary (<= 4 MiB, metres, +Y up) whose origin stands on the ground.

collision.description: A simpler glTF binary used for collision and walking instead of model.

yaw_deg.description: Turn about the vertical axis; default 0.

offset_m.description: Shift from the anchor of the place in metres along the client's local x and z axes.

ground_m.description: The point of the model (x and z in model units, before the turn) that stands on the ground, such as the foot of its stairs; the model's height follows the terrain there. Defaults to the origin.

visible_m.description: Distance up to which the server announces the building; default 600.

at_sea.description: When true, the model stands at mean sea level (ships and floating docks) instead of on the terrain height at ground_m. Default false.

on_water.description: When true, the model floats at the water surface of the place's landscape patch (a river, a pond: boats, floating docks) instead of standing on the bed; on dry ground it stands on the terrain. No collider. Default false.

speed_m_s.description: Metres per second over the water at full speed.

clip.description: The clip of the rider's model played while the vehicle moves; the rider keeps the idle clip without it.

vehicle.description: The structure is a vehicle a player boards (E) and steers over the water at this speed, getting off at a shore. Needs on_water or at_sea. Vehicles differ only in speed and clip; the engine moves them all the same way.

about.description: Knowledge card (id from knowledge.yaml) a player standing at the structure can read, such as an inscribed tablet (POST /story/places/{id}/read). Clients learn it as `readable` on the structure's world object.

achievement.description: Achievement (id from achievements.yaml) the player earns by reading `about` at the structure. Requires `about`.

terrain.description: A landscape patch anchored at the place: real-world relief around the site (river banks, tells), replacing the base terrain and procedural relief inside its rectangle. Heights are decimetres above the anchor's placed height, so the patch is portable between worlds.

heightmap.description: A 16-bit greyscale PNG (at most 4 MiB) whose value 0x8000 is the anchor's placed height; other pixels are decimetres above it.

water.description: An equally sized 16-bit greyscale PNG: 0 is dry land, other pixels the water surface in decimetres above the anchor (0x8000), a river at its historical course.

clear.description: A greyscale PNG of any size (8 or 16 bit, at most 4 million pixels) over the whole rectangle: pixels above zero are built or tilled ground (streets, houses, squares, fields) where the server puts no wild trees, rocks, flowers or animals.

map.description: An RGBA PNG (at most 4 million pixels) over the same rectangle as the heightmap: the map of the place that the client's minimap draws (houses, streets, canals, walls; transparent elsewhere). Row 0 is the north edge of the rectangle in the local frame (z grows south), column 0 the west edge.

extent_m.description: The size of the rectangle in the client's local x and z frame, centred on offset_m.

offset_m.description: The centre of the rectangle from the place anchor in metres along the local x and z axes; the anchor must stay inside the feathered core.

feather_m.description: Width of the margin across which the patch blends into the base terrain; default 100.

visible_m.description: Distance from the patch edge up to which the server announces it; default 1200.

music.description: Track (id from music/*.yaml) that plays in the background while the player is within music_radius_m of the place.

music_radius_m.description: Distance from the place within which its music is heard (fades towards the edge); defaults to radius_m.

wildlife.description: Historical flora and fauna of this place: when the player (and scenery cells) lie within radius_m, the server picks wild trees/plants and land animals from these weighted catalogs instead of the global biome table. clear masks and water rules still apply.

radius_m.description: How far from the place the overlay applies; defaults to radius_m of the place, or 500 m.

density.description: Multiplies spawn presence inside the overlay (1 = same rate as the global grid); default 1.

spawn.description: New characters of the world appear here. At most one place of a disk; with several disks the first one in the order of application wins.

locate.description: Where on the planet the place lies, measured from another place (the real geography of a story): distance_m from `from` in the direction bearing_deg of the map of `from`, that is the frame of its landscape patch and buildings (0 is up the map, north; 90 is east), along a great circle. The planet is not the Earth, so the site is the nearest one within tolerance_m of that point that satisfies the place's `requires`; placement fails when there is none. Not with `at`.

tolerance_m.description: How far from the exact point a site may lie; default a twentieth of the distance, at least 30 m. Zero is a surveyed point: the place stands exactly there, and its `requires` are advice for the author (violations are logged by the server), not a constraint to search around - the water flow is no obstacle to a city.

geo.description: The historical site itself, on the real planet the manifest defines (world.terrain): latitude_deg and longitude_deg in the frame of those rasters (latitude = asin(y), longitude = atan2(-z, x)). The place stands exactly there: history has already decided, so `requires` is advice for the author (violations are logged by the server), not a constraint to search around. Not with `at`, `locate`, `parent` or `near`.

at.description: Fixes the place to a spot of its parent's walled town: the main gate (just inside the wall) or a back alley far from it, out of the gate guard's sight and hearing. Requires a parent with the town preset and size town.

npcs.description: npcs/*.yaml: characters standing at a place.

model.description: A glTF binary below media/models/ (<= 4 MiB) drawn instead of the pack character; pack and skin stay the fallback.

visible_if.description: The character stands in the world, and can be talked to, only for a player of whom this condition holds (a character the story has not brought forth yet is not there). Without it the character is always there.

lift_m.description: Metres above the ground that a character without a walk stands: on the top platform of a ziggurat, whose stairs a player climbs (0 to 200).

about.description: Knowledge card (id from knowledge.yaml) that the character tells when the player asks it to tell about itself. Without it the character offers no such option.

movement.description: The character walks instead of standing at its place. Where it is depends only on its id, its place and the time (nothing is stored); servers send a route of waypoints and clients walk the character along it, with the Walk clip of its model while it moves and Idle while it stands. A character that keeps a shop (tag shop:<id>) cannot walk.

kind.description: wander: walks to spots near its place, standing between walks; patrol: walks the loop of waypoints.

radius_m.description: How far from its place a wanderer goes.

pause_s.description: How long it stands between walks (at each waypoint of a patrol).

follow.description: A patrol that follows the road of a trail of the disk (`id` in trails/*.yaml) to its end and back, instead of listing waypoints: the server takes them from the road once it is laid. Needs kind patrol and no waypoints.

waypoints.description: The loop of a patrol: metres east and south of the place, as offset_m of a building. Not for wanderers.

size.description: How many times taller than the model as authored the character stands (a god towers over men); default 1.

tags.description: Free labels; `shop:<id>` (an id of the server's etc/shops.json, such as shop:general) makes the character a merchant who buys and sells for gold.

branch.description: Automatic routing: the first entry whose condition holds (or has none) is taken; the node shows no text.

goto.description: Next node; omitted ends the conversation.

music.description: Track from music/*.yaml played during the conversation.

river.description: rivers/<name>.yaml: a river (or a list of rivers: a drainage network is hundreds of short ones, each file under a megabyte) of the disk's real planet (needs world.terrain), told as a course of points from its source to its mouth. The server carves a channel into the ground along it and the client draws its water, wherever no landscape patch replaces the ground (a patch carries its own river and the course should pass through it). The coarse planet map has rivers a few tens of metres wide at best; a great river such as the Euphrates is told here.

points.description: [latitude, longitude, width_m] in degrees and metres, downstream: the width of the water at that point (10 to 400 m).

buildings.description: buildings/<name>.yaml: many buildings of the disk around the anchor of one of its places (a city's houses), each drawn from a glTF binary of the disk and standing on the ground. For the few buildings that need a place of their own use the place's structure. The file is data a tool writes (Uruk: tools/build_buildings.py), not text to edit.

place.description: The place whose anchor the positions are measured from.

model.description: A glTF binary (<= 4 MiB, metres, +Y up) whose origin is the middle of its footprint on the ground; its front is +Z.

x.description: Metres east of the anchor of the place.

z.description: Metres south of the anchor of the place (the client's local z axis, as structure.offset_m).

yaw_deg.description: Compass bearing the model's front (+Z) points to: 0 north, 90 east, 180 south.

scale.description: Metres per model unit along the model's x (width), y (height) and z (depth) axes.

footprint.description: Width (along the model's x) and depth (along z) of the plot in metres: the box that blocks walking, and the ground the building is levelled on - the model stands on the lowest terrain under it.

sink_m.description: Metres the model is sunk below the lowest terrain under its plot (default 3; 0 for a passable one, which is sunk below the ground under its middle). Models do not share one floor level, so it is set per model.

passable.description: A thing that lies on the ground and is walked over (a tilled field): it blocks nothing and stands at the height of the ground under its middle.

achievements.description: achievements.yaml: achievements of the disk, shown after the engine's own and qualified as <disk>:<id>. Ids are permanent once released: characters keep what they earned, and a Steam build names each achievement <DISK>__<ID> in capitals, so an id never holds a double underscore. Texts are translation keys of the disk.

id.description: Lowercase letters and digits in words joined by single underscores.

description_key.description: What earns it; a hidden achievement shows it only once earned.

icon.description: An item whose inventory icon the client shows.

hidden.description: Title and description stay secret until it is earned; default false.

read_all.description: Places whose readable structure (`about`) the character must all have read; the achievement is earned with the last one (for example every tablet of one legend).

knowledge.description: knowledge.yaml: knowledge cards that characters tell about themselves or their trade, each with one picture and a link to a Wikipedia article. Texts are translation keys; the client chooses the language of the text and of the article.

text_key.description: A short summary of two to four sentences.

image.description: The picture, a png or jpg below media/knowledge/ (<= 1 MiB).

credit_key.description: Author, work and licence of the picture. Only public-domain or freely licensed pictures may be shipped.

wikipedia.description: Title of the article by language (two lowercase letters); English is required. The link is https://<language>.wikipedia.org/wiki/<title>; underscores for spaces, no ?, #, / or other URL syntax.

quest.description: quests/<name>.yaml: a scenario as a state machine; stages are advanced by dialogue effects.

start_place.description: Place where the quest begins; the aetherglass compass shows it as the next story point until the quest is started.

known_places.description: Places that go on the map and the compass as soon as the quest is begun, and stay there, before any stage points at them.

excerpt.description: Clay-tablet prologue when the quest first appears: spoken paraphrase (narrator voice + bottom subtitles) and optional Latin Akkadian carved as cuneiform on the tablet.

guide.description: Place the aetherglass compass points to during this stage (defaults to the reach place).

reach.description: Moves the quest to stage `goto` when the player comes within radius_m of the place.

fail_restart.description: When the player dies or a quest companion fails during this stage, reset here instead of the quest start_stage/start_place.

lore.description: lore/*.yaml: codex entries (gods, traditions); never spawned.

strings.description: i18n/<language>.yaml: flat map of text keys to text (at most 2000 characters each).

media_path.description: Path of a file inside the datadisk, below media/ (png, jpg or ogg).

music.description: music/*.yaml: tracks (OGG Vorbis) a dialogue can play.

voices.description: voice/voices.yaml: how the build tool (render_voices.py) synthesizes the spoken lines. Not read by the server: the server only serves media/voice/<language>/<text_key>.ogg. A recording at that path always replaces a synthetic line.

models.description: Piper model per language (two lowercase letters).

placeholders.description: What a recording says for a placeholder of the texts, per language: {player} (the name the player chose) is replaced by this form of address. A text key `<key>.say` in i18n replaces the whole text for the voice.

loudness.description: Integrated loudness of the spoken lines in LUFS per language (two lowercase letters); `default` applies to the other languages. The lines of a language are normalised to it; human recordings are not touched.

npcs.description: Per NPC id: a voice profile, plus optional per-language overrides keyed by language.

speaker.description: Speaker id of a multi-speaker model.
